g.text: Receive an allowed response, then verify trusted metadata and signatures locally. Verification failure stops
use; it never approves an artifact.
An admitted miss or stale response reaches the source; cache/privacy rules are respected and the client
verifies before use. Unsigned or expired metadata is rejected unless an explicit trusted-source exception
Run the HTTP refinement and compare observed actions with this sequence.
See what Squid and APT actually did for these retrieval cases.

g.text: Return a retrieval error and stop without content verification.
A source failure after an admitted miss produces no usable content, no client verification and no implicit
stale fallback. The execution model supplies availability; deployed failure behavior needs separate

g.text: Reject cached content before use; a cache hit does not imply trust.
Cached content is verified at the client and rejected when trust fails, without a source fetch. Model trust
is an input, not a cryptographic check.
